items.title: Tom Baker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: And so at the time my hero was Al Hirt.

ctx.x: No, no, I started riding cable cars just kind of kidding myself that if I’d get it cut off I’d play better. But yeah, Wingy Manone was a hero, a trumpet player and of course Louis © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -7-

Armstrong. I remember when I first got to Sydney playing in jazz band, I hadn’t heard Louis Armstrong. I’d seen him on something like “The Dean Martin Show,” a very late appearance, in maybe ‘71 or just before he died. And he didn’t play, he just sang a bit of “Mame” or “Cabaret” or “Hello Dolly,” or one of those things. And I thought, oh, that’s Louis Armstrong? And so at the time my hero was Al Hirt. I remember kind of a dud banjo player who was the band leader, turned around after a couple of nights and said,…
